rationale: Clean objective evidence: the accepted parent step is ~131-139 ms (project.json parent_values; original baseline 136.9/137.0 ms) while observed GPU busy work is far smaller: rank-0 kernel sums in the discovery trace are 8.6 ms forward, ~23.4 ms backward compute (82.8 ms backward minus 59.4 ms NCCL), 1.7 ms optimizer (call-resources 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0), and the 13 bucket allreduces are 12x3.6 ms + 19.5 ms = ~63 ms (nsys rank-1 kernels, back-to-back on stream 17 with ~90 us cross-rank start alignment; collective_calibration medians 3.52/19.50 ms). That accounts for roughly 80 ms of GPU-busy time, leaving on the order of 50 ms of the clean step as host-side dispatch gaps around a few thousand tiny eager kernels (this micro_batch=1, seq=128 eager GPT-2 forward issues long Python view/transpose/split chains per block; nsys shows 25.7 ms of GPU busy spread over 107 ms of pre-communication wall, i.e. a launch-paced compute stream). Communication is not an actionable lever for step_ms here: the 497.8 MB fp32 gradient volume is frozen with the no_sync accumulation pattern (project invariant), the link runs at its observed rate (8.0-8.1 GB/s logical for both 28 MB and 158 MB payloads; RING kernels, 2 channels, SHM transport with peer access disabled and NVLink unsupported), and the previous joint candidate that replaced the two c10d.allreduce_ groups (f833b57a373d8262a384/8525af72c631b94e3dd0) with a Python-orchestrated chunked isend/irecv one-shot exchange was measured at 230.5/234.1 ms versus parent 131.0/139.1 ms and rejected (paired_gain_not_above_noise, objective_not_improved); even its thin Python wrapper added ~2.3 ms per-bucket rank skew (previous-after execution_timeline: rank-1 bucket kernels 5.6 ms vs 3.3 ms). Those two allreduce groups are therefore deliberately excluded. The selected region is the complete eager module stack executed during accumulate_microbatches - GPT2LMHeadModel/GPT2Model/GPT2Block plus the 12 per-block GPT2Attention sites, GPT2MLP, the four Conv1D sites, LayerNorm, NewGELUActivation, lm_head Linear, both Embedding sites and Dropout (151 calls, 26 groups). This is a coherent editable boundary: the stack is invoked identically for all 4 micro-batches, its Python-level dispatch and per-module hook machinery are what pace the compute stream before and during the allreduce window (only ~18 ms of backward compute currently overlaps the ~63 ms comm window), and any rewrite of a parent module necessarily changes the observed child module calls, so the whole stack is selected together rather than as unrelated separate edits.
hypothesis: Replacing the module-boundary execution of the selected stack with a dispatch-minimized implementation that emits the identical eager aten op sequence per micro-batch (a flattened same-order reimplementation, optionally CUDA-graph capture/replay taken lazily inside the actual adapter invocation under the installed parent context, with static input/weight/bucket-view buffers preserved across resets because inputs are pre-generated, reset copies into the same storages, and gradient_as_bucket_view pins grad storage) will remove a large fraction of the ~50 ms host-side gap without changing any kernel or any byte on the wire: numerics stay bitwise identical, so the exact cross-rank gradient check, the 1e-6/1e-4 reference gradient and parameter checks, the finite-loss and negative controls, and the continuous-step/reset semantics are all preserved by construction. Expected effect to be tested: step_ms falls from ~136 ms toward the ~100-110 ms range set by GPU compute (~34 ms) plus the irreducible ~63 ms serialized allreduce tail with its existing ~18 ms overlap; secondary benefits are reduced cross-rank submission skew at the first bucket. The gain is a hypothesis pending the paired A/B measurement: if the clean run is instead GPU- or sync-bound, removing dispatch will not move step_ms and the candidate fails its noise bound.
